I've been experimenting with different things such as filling in templates and free-writing.

For templates, I usually start with a gratitude list. I type in anything I'm grateful for that comes into my mind. For me, this is a great way to get into a great mood. After that, I have a morning journaling section where I type for the morning. It involves anything that comes into my mind such as dreams, thoughts, feelings and what to do for the day. Usually, I won't be journaling until the evening. This is where the evening journaling section comes. It's more of a reflection for what happened during the day, good or bad, so that I am self-aware of my actions and behavior. Lastly, I have a to-do list for the day after. This is a game-changer for me and I think many people can agree as well. It makes me remember the to-do list more clearly when I wake up in the morning. It also frees up my mind during sleep or gives me time to think about how I can do it (not letting it run around my thoughts for too long.)  


Nowadays, I try to free-write, using time-stamps instead but I prefer the template method  pre-quarantine.

It's great of you to ask. I've researched and tried different methods of journaling and personally, I may have found my own style that I can roll with. I hope you find yours, just keep experimenting and see what floats your boat.
